about: BOSS-FCI's and GRaSP-FCI's own published measurements, one file per lane; the release summary's BOSS-FCI and GRaSP-FCI entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 7 November 2026 (version string 0.14.0), the 0.15.0 release branch, where BOSS-FCI and GRaSP-FCI follow the BOSS-FCI paper's Algorithm 5 by default; the option entries ran on the same branch with edge_removal="triangles"
comparator: tetrad-lib 7.6.10's BossFci and GraspFci, the implementation by the methods' authors (gated); causal-cmd 1.12.0's bfci and grasp-fci, tetrad-lib 7.6.3 (context); causal-cmd 1.12.0's bfci and grasp-fci are also the reference of Andrey's edge_removal="triangles" (option), which runs their rule
verdict_rule: per cell, method, and setting: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, the reference's SHD the mean over its runs on that dataset, on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; a row with fewer than 10 paired datasets is reported, not judged; better or worse counts only if a rerun on seeds 100-119 agrees. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). tetrad-lib 7.6.10's BossFci and GraspFci are the gated reference; causal-cmd 1.12.0's bfci and grasp-fci (tetrad-lib 7.6.3) are context (role), reported and never judged; Andrey's boss_fci and grasp_fci with edge_removal="triangles", the rule of Ogarrio, Spirtes, and Ramsey (2016, Sec. 5) that causal-cmd 1.12.0 (tetrad-lib 7.6.3) runs, are judged against causal-cmd's bfci and grasp-fci by the same rule (the entries whose comparator is Tetrad 7.6.3; role option in the lane file), on the in-claim cells; the default rows stay against tetrad-lib 7.6.10
fit_protocol: per dataset, each package in one child process pinned to one core with one BLAS thread; Andrey runs each fit once untimed on the same data first, and Tetrad starts one JVM per run with one untimed warm-up search before the timed one; each Tetrad hybrid runs five times per dataset with no seed (once on the 200-variable cell); a call past its cap (1,800 s; 3,600 s at 100 variables and out of claim) is a timeout, never an empty graph; Andrey's time is the fit from the array in memory, Tetrad's the search inside the JVM; ratio is the median over the paired datasets of the reference's time over Andrey's
error_metric: shd: the endpoint SHD against the PAG of the measured variables (andrey.data.latent.marginal, checked against pcalg's dag2pag on every graph of up to 30 measured variables): variable pairs whose two endpoint marks differ, so a missing or extra edge costs both. andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, the reference's SHD per dataset the mean over its runs, and the _mean fields their means
seeds_note: seeds is the number of datasets per cell on the first seeds: 20 (seeds 0-19) in P20 and P100, 10 (seeds 0-9) in O1 and O3, and 1 (seed 0) in O2, which measures time only. 10 cells with a row better or worse on the first seeds reran both packages' gated arms on seeds 100-119 (replication)
